statement: You are given a string s.
Rearrange its characters so that they are in decreasing order of how often they occur in s, with all copies of the same character kept together.
Return the rearranged string. Characters that occur equally often may come in either order, so more than one answer can be correct.

examples.explanation: e occurs twice and comes first; r and t occur once each. "eetr" would also be correct.
a and c both occur three times, so either block may come first; "cccaaa" is equally correct. Mixing them, as in "cacaca", is not.

constraints: s consists of uppercase and lowercase English letters and digits
